Aryne-mediated [2,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement
of tertiary 2,3-allenylamines bearing an
electron-withdrawing group at the α-position†
Lu Han, Xue-Ting Zhang, Dong Xie and Shi-Kai Tian
 *
An unprecedented [2,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement reaction of quaternary 2,3-allenylammonium ylides,
generated in situ from tertiary 2,3-allenylamines and arynes, has been established. With 2-(trimethylsilyl)
aryl tri ﬂates as aryne precursors, a range of tertiary 2,3-allenylamines bearing an electron-withdrawing
group at the α-position smoothly participated in the aryne-mediated [2,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement at
room temperature, delivering structurally diverse 2-vinylallyamines or 1-amino-1,3-dienes in moderate to
excellent yields. The reaction proceeds in the absence of strong bases and transition metals, is compatible
with moisture and air, and tolerates a wide variety of functional groups.
Introduction
Owing to charge acceleration, transformation of tertiary
amines into the corresponding quaternary ammonium ylides,
bearing an electron-withdrawing group at the α-position, sig-
nificantly reduces the reaction temperature for the sigmatropic
rearrangements via C–N bond cleavage, permitting the process
to serve as a key step in the construction of complex nitrogen-
containing molecules.
1 In this regard, a number of quaternary
allyl-, propargyl-, and benzylammonium ylides have been
reported to be prepared via stepwise or one-pot quaternization
of tertiary amines followed by deprotonation, and participate
in a [2,3]- or a [1,2]-sigmatropic rearrangement to a ﬀord func-
tionalized tertiary amines that are not readily synthesized by
alternative methods (Scheme 1a). Nevertheless, to our knowl-
edge, it remains unexplored for the sigmatropic rearrangement
of quaternary 2,3-allenylammonium ylides, which would yield
2-vinylallylamines as promising versatile building blocks in
chemical synthesis through transformations such as oxidation,
carbonylation, and cycloaddition (Scheme 1b).
2
Arynes have recently emerged as powerful electrophiles to
activate tertiary allyl-, 3 propargyl-,4 and benzylamines 5 bearing
an electron-withdrawing group at the α-position under mild
conditions to generate in situ the corresponding quaternary
ammonium ylides, 6 which participate in sigmatropic
rearrangements to produce various aniline derivatives. In con-
trast to the in situ generation of quaternary ammonium ylides
via transition metal-catalyzed N-alkylation of tertiary allyl- 7 or
propargylamines with diazo compounds 8 or allylic carbonates 9
or via zinc halide-catalyzed ring-opening of epoxides by tertiary
amines,10 the aryne-mediated sigmatropic rearrangements of
tertiary amines avoids the employment of transition metals,
and moreover, introduces N-aryl groups into the target mole-
cules. In this context, we envisioned that similar addition of
tertiary 2,3-allenylamines bearing an electron-withdrawing
group at the α-position to arynes followed by proton transfer
would lead to the formation of quaternary 2,3-allenylammo-
nium ylides, which would undergo a [2,3]-sigmatropic
rearrangement to yield 2-vinylallyamines (Scheme 2). Care
should be taken to prevent the aryl group from participating in
an aromatic aza-Claisen rearrangement.
11 In exposure to a
base, some of the 2-vinylallyamine products would further iso-
merize to 1-amino-1,3-dienes. 4a

Results and discussion
In the model reaction of N-(2,3-allenyl)glycine ester 1a with
benzyne in acetonitrile at room temperature without extrusion
of moisture and air, we surveyed a few readily available fluoride
sources for the in situ generation of benzyne via fluoride-
induced 1,2-elimination of 2-(trimethylsilyl)phenyl triflate ( 2a)
(Table 1, entries 1 –8).12 The use of TBAF predominantly
aﬀorded 1-amino-1,3-diene 3a′ (3a : 3a′ = 2 : 98) as a
53 : 47 mixture of Z- and E-isomers (Table 1, entry 6), and in
sharp contrast, combined use of KF and 18-crown-6 a ﬀorded
2-vinylallyamine 3a as a major isomer ( 3a : 3a′ = 84 : 16)
(Table 1, entry 8). Obviously, isomerization of 2-vinylallyamine
3a to 1-amino-1,3-diene 3a′ occurred under the weak basic con-
ditions.4a In these cases, the phenyl group was not observed to
participate in an aromatic aza-Claisen rearrangement. We then
examined a number of solvents (Table 1, entries 9 –14), and to
our delight, found that performing the reaction in tetrahydro-
furan enhanced the ratio between 2-vinylallyamine 3a and
1-amino-1,3-diene 3a′ from 84 : 16 to 96 : 4 as well as the com-
bined yield from 70% to 79% (Table 1, entry 9). Moreover, sig-
nificant isomerization of 2-vinylallyamine 3a to 1-amino-1,3-
diene 3a′ was observed after prolonging the reaction time from
3 h to 20 h (Table 1, entry 15).
Under the optimized conditions, we observed broad sub-
strate scope for the tertiary 2,3-allenylamines in the [2,3]-sig-
matropic rearrangement reaction using 2-(trimethylsilyl)
phenyl triflate ( 2a) as a benzyne precursor (Table 2). In
addition to ester groups, the p-nitrophenyl group served as an
electron-withdrawing group in the benzyne-mediated [2,3]-sig-
matropic rearrangement of a tertiary 2,3-allenylamine albeit
the resulting 2-vinylallyamine 3d was isolated in a moderate
yield (Table 2, entry 4). Replacing the ester group with an
amide group did not lead to the formation of the desired
rearrangement product (Table 2, entry 5).
13 When the reaction
was extended to a tertiary 2,3-allenylamine bearing a ketone or
a cyano group, the 1-amino-1,3-diene product rather than the
2-vinylallyamine product was obtained due to ready isomeriza-
tion under the standard conditions (Table 2, entries 6 –8).
While the N-(2,3-allenyl)glycine ester bearing an N-alkyl group
participated in the benzyne-mediated [2,3]-sigmatropic
rearrangement to a ﬀord the corresponding 2-vinylallyamines
in good yields, the reaction of an N-phenyl-containing ana-
logue gave a complex mixture and no rearrangement product
was isolated (Table 2, entries 9 –11). The rearrangement reac-
tion worked well with the N-(2,3-allenyl)glycine esters bearing
a disubstituted or a trisubstituted allenyl group, but significant
erosion of enantiopurity was observed in the axial-to-central
chirality transfer (Table 2, entries 12 –16). In contrast,
L-proline-derived 2,3-allenylamine 1q participated in the
benzyne-mediated [2,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement, construct-
ing a nitrogen-substituted quaternary stereocenter with excel-
lent retention of enantiopurity (Table 2, entry 17). In this case,
high eﬃciency of central-to-central chirality transfer should be
attributable to the highly diastereoselective attack of the cyclic
tertiary amine on benzyne.
We further investigated the migratory tendency of allyl, pro-
pargyl, and benzyl relative to 2,3-allenyl in the benzyne-
mediated sigmatropic rearrangements of tertiary amines
under the standard conditions. In the reaction of N-(2,3-
allenyl)-N-allylglycine ester 1r with benzyne, both of 2,3-allenyl
and allyl participated in the [2,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement
to a ﬀord 2-vinylallyamine 3r and homoallylamine 4a, respect-
ively, in a ratio of 43 : 57 (Scheme 3a). In contrast, the propar-
gyl group was kept untouched in the benzyne-mediated [2,3]-
sigmatropic rearrangement of N-(2,3-allenyl)-N-propargylgly-
cine ester 1s under the standard conditions, probably owing to
unfavourable formation of an envelope-like transition state
from a linear propargyl group relative to a 2,3-allenyl group
(Scheme 3b).
1 Finally, benzyl was found to be reluctant to
migrate relative to 2,3-allenyl, and only 20% of N-(2,3-allenyl)-

A few aryne precursors, 2-(trimethylsilyl)aryl triflates, were
examined with regard to their potential in promoting the [2,3]-
sigmatropic rearrangement of N-(2,3-allenyl)glycine ester 1a
(Table 3). In the reaction of an in situ generated unsymmetrical
aryne, the regioselectivity highly depends on the position of
substituents. In line with previous reports,
14 a single regio-
isomer was obtained from the reaction of 3-methylbenzyne
(Table 3, entry 1), and the amine addition to 4-methylbenzyne
exhibited poor regioselectivity (Table 3, entry 2). A few sym-
metrical arynes were found to mediate the [2,3]-sigmatropic
rearrangement of N-(2,3-allenyl)glycine ester 1a, delivering the
corresponding 2-vinylallyamines in good yields (Table 3,
entries 3 –5). Nevertheless, the reaction of 2,3-pyridyne gave a

Conclusions
In summary, we have established an unprecedented [2,3]-sig-
matropic rearrangement reaction of quaternary 2,3-allenylam-
monium ylides, generated in situ via nucleophilic addition of
tertiary 2,3-allenylamines to arynes, under mild conditions.
Using 2-(trimethylsilyl)aryl triflates as aryne precursors, a
range of tertiary 2,3-allenylamines bearing an electron-with-
drawing group at the α-position smoothly participated in the
aryne-mediated [2,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement at room temp-
erature, delivering structurally diverse 2-vinylallyamines or
1-amino-1,3-dienes in moderate to excellent yields. The reac-
tion proceeds in the absence of strong bases and transition
metals, is compatible with moisture and air, and tolerates a
wide variety of functional groups.
